explanation: Reject negatives and nonzero values ending in zero. Reverse only the last half of the digits, then compare the halves; for odd lengths, discard the reversed half’s middle digit. Reversing only half avoids overflowing a 32-bit integer.
timeComplexity: O(log(x + 1)) time for nonnegative x. Each iteration removes or compares a pair of decimal digits.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only a few integer values or masks are retained.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: After moving the same number of digits from the end into reversed, x is the untouched first half and reversed is the original last half read backward. At the midpoint, equal halves prove an even palindrome; removing reversed’s middle digit handles an odd palindrome. Negative numbers and nonzero trailing-zero numbers cannot be palindromes.
walkthrough: For 4554, the first update gives x=455 and reversed=4. The next gives x=45 and reversed=45, so the halves match and the answer is true.
edgeCases: A nonzero number ending in zero cannot match its first digit.
Reversing only half avoids full-number reversal overflow.
